title: GraphMemix — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn. Each node states both sides; the lane says which stage of the pipeline the divergence sits in. A3 ADMIT is absent from both sides — not drawn, not a divergence.
source: Li et al. 2026 (arXiv:2608.26983v1, MemoraX AI Research)  ×  repo graphmemix @ d0ea01d  ·  servers/graphmemix/verification.md §5 (D1–D14): 12 of 14 drawn — D12 excluded per verification.md's own C52 note, D14 excluded as an eval-only ablation artifact
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: A3 ADMIT holds no nodes on either side and is intentionally not drawn: the paper defines no dedup/conflict/eviction step, and the code's only write-time guard is a memory_id idempotency check, not similarity-based admission — a shared absence, not a divergence.

The most consequential divergence sits at B4: the paper presents the node-utility formula as one fixed closed-form 'equivalent up to displayed rounding' to (α,τ,δ)=(0.8,5.2,0.7), but the shipped coefficients are gold-label-fitted via an undescribed 5-fold SHA256 calibration protocol and do not equal the paper's derived numbers (D7+D8) — and part of that fitted feature vector (D9's standardization fields) is dead code even in the shipping pipeline.

The most quantitatively falsifiable divergence is the ATM schema-relation gap: the paper's Table 6 states 6.23 average Fixed Edges for ATM, but static trace of the ATM converter plus the code's two generic relation rules (D1) — missing all three paper-named relation types (D2) — yields 0 schema edges for that dataset.

D12 (w^schema typed vs a global 0.99 constant) is deliberately excluded: verification.md's own corroboration entry C52 shows the paper itself hardcodes the identical single 0.99 ceiling (txt:1258, txt:1471), so this is a tension between Eq.9's notation and the paper's own stated implementation, not a paper↔code conflict.
